title: IS12:: qpa.c (117.1)

lines.explanation: Using symbolic constants to define MINQPA and MINISQPA is a good programming style and allows for easy changeability of the program.
An empty line separating declarations from the rest of the program improves readability
We read a floating point value into a floating point variable qpa1 using %f specification
We read a floating point value into a floating point variable qpa2 using %f specification
The first condition to check - entered general QPA is matched against the admission threshold

lines.code: printf("Your general QPA is too low for BSIS\n");
lines.explanation: First of the three possible outcomes - you can't be admitted due to low general QPA

Even if you general QPA is over the threshold, it is not yet clear whether you can be admitted - it depends on your IS QPA. So, we need another conditional statement in else part of the first if. This is a standard else-if multiple selection construct. To

lines.code: printf("Your Information Science QPA is too low for BSIS\n");
lines.explanation: Second of the three possible outcomes - you can't be admitted due to low IS QPA

lines.code: else /* here qpa1 >= MINQPA and qpa2 >= MINISQPA */
lines.explanation: This is else part of the embedded if, but we use the same indentation as for original if to stress that it is not just one if inside another - it is an else-if construct
